articles.headline: NFL reassigns backup refs to work games closer to home
articles.description: The NFL, trying to avoid further travel issues from Friday's FAA ground stop, has reassigned officials to Week 10 games within driving distance of their homes.
articles.body:
The NFL, in trying to avoid further travel issues stemming from the FAA ground stop on Friday, has adjusted its officiating assignments for domestic games in Week 10, reassigning officials to games within driving distance of their hometowns.

Airlines across the U.S. worked Saturday to recover from the longest nationwide ground stop in 25 years that canceled more than 2,000 flights, spread ripple effects around the world, stranded passengers and forced professional and college sports teams to scramble for alternate transportation.

The NFL's changes mean three backup referees -- umpires Barry Anderson and Duane Heydt and side judge Don Willard -- will work as referees on Sunday.

Heydt will be at the Carolina-New Orleans game, while Anderson will serve as referee for the Jacksonville-Tennessee tilt.

Willard will serve double-duty on Sunday -- at the Miami-Indianapolis game at 1 p.m. ET and then travel approximately 110 miles to work the Pittsburgh-Cincinnati game, which kicks off at 8:20 p.m. ET on Sunday night.

The NFL said each of the league's 17 officiating crews have a backup referee identified, and that individual trains throughout the year to work at the referee position should the need arise.

The nationwide stop, attributed to new technology being added to the nation's air traffic control system and causing "intermittent" communications and radar gaps, was the second since the Sept. 11, 2001, attacks.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

articles.headline: Sources: Vikings made initial Kirk Cousins trade call to Raiders before MNF
articles.description: The Vikings initially reached out to the Raiders about a Kirk Cousins trade before their MNF game against the Bills, sources told ESPN and NFL Network.
articles.body:
The first time the Vikings reached out to the Raiders about a potential trade for Kirk Cousins was midday Monday, hours before Minnesota played the Bills on "Monday Night Football," league sources told ESPN and NFL Network.

During that call, the Vikings made it clear to the Raiders that they wanted to see how Monday night went first before having any further conversations about Cousins, but they would be in touch if needed.

Bright and early the next morning, hours after Minnesota's offensive meltdown, the Vikings called the Raiders before 6 a.m. PT and setting the wheels in motion for a potential Cousins trade.

It was not a deal the Raiders wanted or were looking to make, especially when Minnesota's initial offer was a fifth-round draft pick, according to sources.

But once the Vikings upped their offer to a third-round pick, the Raiders had discussions about whether the trade made sense, and here's where they landed:

Not only would they be receiving a third-round pick, but they also would be freeing up $10 million in cash for the 2027 season, as the bonus guarantee owed to Cousins would shift to Minnesota's responsibility. It was not a trade that the Raiders enjoyed making, but it was one they believed would be in the best interests of the organization.

The Raiders also believed 2026 No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza has looked, in the word of one source, "phenomenal" in practice. There never was going to be a right time to insert Mendoza into the starting lineup, but Minnesota made this as good a time as any.

Cousins will start Sunday against the Packers at Lambeau Field, and Mendoza will make his first career start against the defending Super Bowl champion Seahawks.

Competition committee to discuss trade snafus

The NFL's competition committee is expected to discuss a potential solution after multiple trades this week were voided or altered, according to sources.

In the last week alone, the Bengals declined to make a deal for linebacker Arnold Ebiketie after agreeing to terms on a trade with the Eagles; the Lions and Jets altered the compensation they initially agreed to in a trade for safety Andre Cisco; and the Broncos voided a trade with the Chargers for Daiyan Henley after concerns about the linebacker's knee, and the sides were unable to agree to revised compensation.

Last offseason, the Raiders and Ravens agreed to a Maxx Crosby trade before the star pass rusher failed his physical and the trade was voided.

Now front office executives are complaining, and the competition committee is expected to address the issue during the offseason.

Various front office executives last week pointed out that trade terms should not be negotiable once they are agreed to, as the Lions attempted to do in a deal for Cisco and the Broncos attempted to do with Henley.

Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh said as much to reporters Thursday, asserting that the loophole in the NFL's trade system needs to be closed so that teams cannot back out of deals.

articles.headline: Mauricio Pochettino to Man United: Is Tottenham love affair finally over?
articles.description: Mauricio Pochettino is back in the Premier League as the new Man United boss. For Tottenham fans, it's complicated.
articles.body:
"He's magic, you know, Mauricio Pochettino!" For five years, these were the words that rang out amongst Tottenham fans.

First, at the old White Hart Lane -- a much-loved, if dilapidated, ground that became a fortress during Pochettino's years as head coach of the club. Then, at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium -- a magnificent arena that, in recent years, has felt more like a house of horrors than any sort of stronghold.

But now Pochettino is back in the Premier League, this time as Manchester United manager. And for Tottenham fans who once dreamed of seeing the Argentine return to north London, it's another reminder that the man who gave us so many unforgettable memories might never be coming home.

The Pochettino love affair

The Argentine manager joined Tottenham in 2014 and was at the helm of one of the best, and most beloved, Spurs teams in the club's history. Under Pochettino, Harry Kane (now a Ballon d'Or winner!), Son Heung-Min, Christian Eriksen, Dele Alli, Jan Vertonghen, Toby Alderweireld, Mousa Dembélé and Hugo Lloris all shone in ways that few football fans and pundits expected.

During the Pochettino era, Tottenham came agonisingly close to winning the Premier League and reached the Champions League final. They went an entire season unbeaten at home -- somewhat unthinkable now given the team's struggles at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium -- and played some of the most thrilling football in the league at the time.

There were famous victories over arch-rivals Arsenal and in Europe, including over Real Madrid and Borussia Dortmund, and, of course, there was that night in Amsterdam. When Lucas Moura scored an astonishing hat trick against Ajax to send Spurs to the Champions League final for the first time in our history.

For many Spurs fans, including myself, the Poch years brought some of our best ever memories of supporting the club. There was a special connection between Pochettino and fans. He was revered and many of us hoped that it would last forever -- even if we all knew that, really, nothing ever lasts that long. Especially not in football.

When Pochettino was sacked, rather unceremoniously, in November 2019 -- just months after taking us to the Champions League final -- it felt somewhat unjust.

It was clear for anyone to see in 2019 that Tottenham's squad was beginning to get stale in a number of areas and that what the club truly needed was a rebuild. For myriad reasons, that never came to fruition and so, when, results on the pitch took a nosedive in the winter of that year the axe fell on Pochettino.

Overnight, the man who had turned Tottenham into a truly formidable side capable of beating anyone on their day was gone. Since then, it's fair to say that no other manager that has taken the wheel at the club has managed to form the same sort of bond that Pochettino had with us.

Many have come and gone but it hasn't yet felt like any of them have "got" us the way that Pochettino did. It is early days under Roberto De Zerbi

articles.headline: The price of a pro hoop dream starts with a $200 G League tryout
articles.description: Former college players, content creators and even some Sixers fans chased the same opportunity to get noticed by the Delaware Blue Coats.
articles.body:
"AIN'T NO WAY," I muttered to myself. If the social media post on my timeline was to be believed, everybody and their cousin could try out for the G League.

The real kicker? It would only cost them $200.

That realization sparked a question: How hard is it to actually make the NBA's G League?

When I posed the question to my editors, they hit me with a challenge: Why don't you find out?

An idea was unlocked. I would participate in an open tryout for the G League. I was up for the challenge. After all, it wouldn't be the first time I took part in this type of experiential journalism. (Last October, I took a trip to Diamond Gym to put my mental and physical endurance to the test by working out at the "Most Dangerous Gym in America"). The assignment would also allow me to tap into a childhood dream.

The game is something that has always been in my DNA. My grandfather ran recreational centers around Kansas City, Kansas. He held winter and summer leagues that I started playing in at the age of 5. Summers consisted of playing in AAU tournaments against some of the nation's top programs with ranked talent like three-time Nike Peach Jam champion MOKAN Elite and KC Run GMC, while winters were for high school basketball. But once high school was over and scholarships for other opportunities outside of basketball poured in, my hoop dreams ended. I would still play in adult leagues (and toast my competition), but if I wanted to be pro-ready, I needed pro advice.

My uncle Earl Watson, a retired 13-season NBA veteran and former NBA head coach, was the person I called for coaching advice on what they might look for in a prospect.

"They want who wants it most and plays the game with respect," Watson said.

Watson saw firsthand where a paid open tryout could lead. He began his coaching career with the Austin Spurs, San Antonio's G League affiliate. That's where he coached Jonathon Simmons, who paid $150 to try out alongside 60 other players and earned a roster spot in what was then the NBA Development League. Simmons signed his first NBA contract with San Antonio in July 2015 and went on to land a three-year, $20 million deal with the Orlando Magic.

Watson likened the tryout process to the Jordan Peele-produced psychological horror movie "Him" and the needed mentality to a notable line from the film: "What are you willing to sacrifice?"

THE NEXT ORDER of business was finding a tryout. As fate would have it, the Delaware Blue Coats, affiliate of the Philadelphia 76ers -- and coincidentally the same team my NBA 2K27 MyPlayer plays for -- were hosting an open tryout in a couple of weeks. Maybe this was a sign.

According to Blue Coats head coach JP Clark, every year the team holds an open tryout to give talent exposure to Delaware's front office and staff, as well as 76ers scouts.

As for what he looks for in said tryout?

"What we're looking for is just talent, right? Just talented players that are good people, good character, that can bring value to our tea

articles.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Como's Nico Paz to be Pochettino's first Man United summer signing?
articles.description: Manchester United are monitoring Como superstar Nico Paz ahead of a move next summer. Transfer Talk has the latest.
articles.body:
Manchester United are monitoring Como superstar Nico Paz ahead of a move next summer, while Chelsea are considering a January swoop for Barcelona defender Jules Koundé. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Trending rumors

- Manchester United are monitoring Como superstar Nico Paz ahead of a move next summer, according to The Sun. The 22-year-old was already on United's radar before scoring twice and providing an assist against them in the UEFA Champions League last month. Mauricio Pochettino's arrival as manager could help their pursuit of his fellow Argentine, although Real Madrid retain an €80 million option to re-sign the midfielder in 2027. Meanwhile, The Telegraph says that Pochettino is expected to be backed in the January transfer window, with the Red Devils likely to be in the market for a defender and a striker.

Barca are open to the 28-year-old's departure as they seek to raise funds for their own transfer plans, while Chelsea have been assessing the feasibility of any future deal. Despite interest from Saudi Arabia, Koundé would prefer to remain in Europe, with the Premier League his priority. A move to London is also understood to appeal to the France international.

- Liverpool and Bayern Munich are monitoring Stuttgart defender Finn Jeltsch, according to Christian Falk. Liverpool scouts have recently watched the 20-year-old, who is also on the radar of several other Premier League clubs. His ability to operate at both center back and right back has helped him earn a place in Germany's squad. However, Falk believes a move to England is unlikely to be Jeltsch's next step as he looks to progress gradually.

- Real Madrid are monitoring Atlético Mineiro center back Vitão, with Brighton and Everton also interested, Sport reports. Brighton are expected to make the first formal approach for the 18-year-old in January, with a proposed €14 million offer falling below his €20 million release clause for overseas clubs. Atlético Mineiro have attempted to extend the Brazilian's contract to increase that clause, but negotiations have stalled in recent weeks.

The proposed agreement contains no release clause, while his annual salary would rise from approximately €2.5 million gross to around €4 million plus bonuses. articles.description: Touchdown for Chuba Hubbard? Fantasy upside for Aaron Rodgers? Trick play from the Raiders? Let's predict 15 things for Week 10.

Week 10 of the 2026 NFL season is underway after the Commanders beat the Giants on Thursday night. But what will happen in the remaining 13 games? We have 15 predictions from our NFL experts.

First, betting analyst Pamela Maldonado picks two underdogs who could win outright. Then, analytics writer Seth Walder projects stat lines for three players. Fantasy football writer Eric Moody suggests three sleepers, and analyst Matt Bowen predicts three players who will find the end zone. Finally, analyst Ben Solak lays out four wild-card predictions.

Will the Steelers upset the Bengals? How many yards will Trey McBride have against the Rams? Could Jadarian Price score his first NFL touchdown? And will Raiders coach Klint Kubiak dial up a trick play in Fernando Mendoza's first start?

Let's make 15 big predictions for the Sunday and Monday action.

Jump to:

Upset picks | Projected stat lines

Maldonado predicts two upsets

Carolina Panthers +2.5 (+110 moneyline) at New Orleans Saints

Quarterback Bryce Young is getting the ball out more quickly recently without sacrificing chances downfield, which could be helpful against New Orleans' pass rush. The Saints are allowing 7.8 yards per pass attempt, giving Tetairoa McMillan opportunities to make big plays.

New Orleans hasn't gotten much from its running game, and it will be without starting center Erik McCoy (biceps injury) on Sunday. That puts more stress on quarterback Tyler Shough, enabling Carolina to keep this close and potentially win outright.

Pittsburgh Steelers +3.5 (+150 moneyline) at Cincinnati Bengals

Running back Jaylen Warren gives Pittsburgh a way to control this game. He already piled up 176 total yards in Pittsburgh's Week 3 win over Cincinnati, and the Bengals keep giving up long runs this season.

Cincinnati also struggles to defend the middle of the field, where Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers has strong options in WR Germie Bernard and TE Darnell Washington. Bengals QB Joe Burrow will get his points, but Pittsburgh can answer without asking Rodgers to force deep throws.

articles.headline: Untold stories of Detroit Lions WR Amon-Ra St. Brown's German upbringing
articles.description: For Amon-Ra St. Brown, Sunday's NFL game in Munich will mark the ultimate convergence of his dual heritage. Here are stories that shed more light.
articles.body:
DETROIT -- When the Detroit Lions take the field to face the New England Patriots at Allianz Arena in Munich on Sunday, wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown will feel right at home.

For St. Brown, Germany is as much his home as the United States. It's where he and his family frequently took trips to visit his maternal grandparents. It's where St. Brown went to preschool (Die Rheinpiraten Kindergarten, to be exact), and where he and his older brothers, Equanimeous and Osiris, spent countless hours on bike tours and fishing trips with their grandfather, Helmut Steyer, who enjoyed entertaining his American-born grandsons.

It's where Amon-Ra (and Osiris) was a standout for the country's under-19 national football team. It's where he has hosted football camps since becoming a pro in 2021. And it's where the Lions star was once asked by an uncle to stay in order to become a star in the other type of football.

"It's not strange to him. It's all familiar ... everything," St. Brown's mother, Miriam Brown, said. "Going to restaurants, everything is different but for him it's familiar."

The deep connection and familiarity St. Brown has with the country is because of Miriam. Born and raised in Leverkusen, in western Germany, she instilled her German values into Amon-Ra and his brothers, who are all fluent in German.

Those values, and experiences, are a part of St. Brown's identity and have always been at the forefront of who he is. As a result, when the Lions face the Patriots in one of the country's most famous arenas (9:30 a.m. ET on Fox), St. Brown will be the headline act.

More than 80 NFL players who were born in Germany (West Germany and East Germany included) have appeared in a game, per ESPN Research, including 10 who have debuted since 2018. Although he was born in Anaheim Hills, California, few have experienced as much popularity in Germany as St. Brown, who, according to NFL Germany general manager Alexander Steinforth, is the subject of multiple documentaries currently being produced there.

"He's probably the poster boy for the NFL in the German-speaking world these days," Steinforth told ESPN. "He works a lot and has worked a lot with our local broadcast partners, so it's amazing to see when he's kind of talking to his German fans. He's a really big and important name for us here in Germany."

St. Brown wears decals of both the German and American flags on his helmet. He says he's fortunate and proud to be so immersed in both cultures, each of which he has drawn from throughout his life.

"Being half German, half American you kind of get to experience both cultures, and you admire different things in both cultures," St. Brown said. "You feel as if, you know, some things you wish the Americans would do more, some things you wish the Germans would do more.

"But I'm both, so I can pick and choose what I like from each culture. And I think both cultures have amazing, amazing qualities. But I'm just glad that I was able to dip my feet into both cu

articles.headline: Falcons insist winning still the goal despite trading Jessie Bates III
articles.description: Atlanta wanted to ensure trading away Jessie Bates III didn't send the wrong message to the team.
articles.body:
FLOWERY BRANCH, Ga. -- Overcommunication. That has been the order of business over the past several days for Atlanta Falcons coach Kevin Stefanski.

That has included one-on-one meetings with players, small-group conversations with the team's player leadership committee and full team meetings. Stefanski has wanted to make it absolutely certain that the Falcons, despite trading two starters before the NFL trade deadline earlier this week, are not in any way giving up on this season.

"I would tell you we've got a great group of leadership on this team," Stefanski said. "I've talked to them a lot over the last few days -- like I do all the time, but in particular now. I'm very, very confident in their leadership."

On Monday, the Falcons traded All-Pro safety Jessie Bates III to the Jacksonville Jaguars for a 2027 second-round draft pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick. Bates, aside from being arguably the best safety in the league, was also a team captain and one of the most respected veterans in the building.

A day later, Atlanta traded starting center Ryan Neuzil to the Baltimore Ravens for reserve guard Andrew Vorhees and a 2028 sixth-round pick. Neuzil was a Falcons success story, starting with the team as an undrafted free agent and working his way up to a starting role.

The Falcons are 3-6. So, in that respect, it made perfect sense to get value back for two players who were set to become free agents in the offseason. With regards to Bates, a safety had not been acquired for a second-round pick since 2018. Few could blame Atlanta for making the move.

"We believe the return gives us a meaningful opportunity to strengthen this roster over time," a team source said. "That does not mean Jessie stopped being an outstanding player. We are giving up something valuable and we understand that."

On the other hand, the Falcons are in one of the most unique positions in the NFL. Their record is ugly, but they are a half-game out of first place in a weak NFC South. All four teams in the division are sitting at three wins apiece. Atlanta finishes its season playing its NFC South rivals back-to-back-to-back.

So, there was also an argument for standing pat and making a good-faith run at the playoffs, where the Falcons have not been since 2017. Only the New York Jets have a longer drought.

"We're still in it," quarterback Michael Penix Jr. said. "... We're so close in a lot of areas and I feel like in this organization we view that a lot. We use that a lot. We are so close.

"I truly believe we have the team and the guys that's going to rally and flip the script because we got a lot of guys that care. Obviously, I feel like matchup wise, I feel like our team is one of the top teams in the league."

articles.headline: Why the Raiders named Fernando Mendoza as the starter
articles.description: The Raiders named Fernando Mendoza as the starter shortly after trading Kirk Cousins to the Vikings.
articles.body:
HENDERSON, Nev. -- There isn't a particular moment that convinced the Las Vegas Raiders players and coaches that No. 1 pick Fernando Mendoza was ready to be the team's starting quarterback. It's a collection of things the rookie has done since he arrived at the facility in April.

For coach Klint Kubiak, it's Mendoza's improvement in his accuracy and knowledge of the offense each week. A month ago, backup quarterback Aidan O'Connell recalled watching Mendoza make a few throws in practice, causing him to turn to quarterbacks coach Mike Sullivan and assistant head coach Mike McCoy and say, "Those were incredible."

Wide receiver Tre Tucker, on the other hand, knew Mendoza was capable of being QB1 when he watched the College Football Playoff National Championship game this past January and saw him lower his shoulder to knock off a Miami defender before diving into the end zone for a touchdown that helped Indiana secure its first-ever title.

"That shows you the kind of guy we are getting," Tucker said.

On Tuesday, Mendoza was named the starting quarterback after the Raiders traded veteran Kirk Cousins to the Minnesota Vikings. The Raiders' decision to move on from Cousins sent shock waves through the locker room. But with Mendoza, the first quarterback taken by the Raiders in the first round since 2007, waiting in the wings, the team knew this moment would come at some point.

As abrupt as the change of power might have felt, the Raiders believe Mendoza is ready for his starting debut Sunday against the Seattle Seahawks, the reigning Super Bowl champs and one of the league's most menacing defenses.

"Obviously there's a learning curve there, but Fernando is someone who just works extremely hard," starting center Tyler Linderbaum said. "... Anytime you get that with someone who wants to be great, and then on top of that has great mentors with them, I think it's very important. He's ready. We're ready."

The Raiders might have been more hesitant to move on from Cousins, who is second in the league in touchdown passes this season, if they felt Mendoza couldn't handle the role. To that point, Kubiak doesn't plan to make things easy for Mendoza in his debut.

Kubiak won't hold anything back from Mendoza and believes the 23-year-old signal-caller can operate the entire playbook. That confidence comes from Mendoza preparing as if he was the starter since Week 1.

"One of our mottos in the quarterback room is to always stay ready and always stay prepared," Mendoza said. "All three of us prepared like the starter. We were all in there doing our routine, doing it together, watching film together, going over the game plan together, tweaking and seeing which adjustments we'd like to make."

Mendoza went above and beyond to make sure he was ready in case his number was called. During games, Mendoza stood hip-to-hip with Sullivan. He wore his helmet while relaying the calls to Sullivan as delivered through the helmet communication device.

articles.headline: Man United, Pochettino's to-do list based on what's gone wrong this season
articles.description: Pochettino makes as much sense as anyone to take the Man United job, so now what? Let's look at the mess he's inheriting and what's at the top of his to-do list.
articles.headlineJa: マンチェスター・ユナイテッド、今季の不調から紐解くポチェッティーノの課題リスト
articles.descriptionJa: ポチェッティーノはマンチェスター・ユナイテッドの監督に就任するのにふさわしい人物の一人だが、次は何をすべきか。彼が引き継ぐ混乱した状況と、最優先課題について考察する。
articles.body:
What has been your favorite mind-boggling decision of Manchester United's lost era? Mine was when they hired Ralf Rangnick to establish modern pressing-and-possession principles for half a season ... three months after signing Cristiano Ronaldo, the most anti-pressing-and-possession star of the modern era. Shockingly, it wasted everyone's time (though Rangnick still averaged more points per game than Ruben Amorim).

Given everything we've learned about running a properly functional soccer club in the 2020s, it's nice to have a strong "Don't be like [insert club name here]" at which to point.

You're supposed to use your front office to establish the direction and identity of the club, then hire the coach to follow that identity; the era of the "Great Man" manager is over. But Manchester United, the club that owes its modern success (and valuation) to the greatest Great Man manager of the past 50 years (Sir Alex Ferguson), can't help but search for the next Fergie at all times.

You aren't supposed to constantly hire the stylistic opposite of your ex, especially if you're giving the new hire too much power over player acquisitions: If you do, you'll end up with a squad of mishmashed parts acquired for all sorts of different purposes. But that seems to be all Manchester United know to do. They lurched from the defense-and-counter David Moyes to the ultracautious, all-possession Louis van Gaal, back to the mostly negative Jose Mourinho, then to the positive (and probably too adaptive) Ole Gunnar Solskjaer.

- Ogden: Man United have finally hired a proper manager

- Dawson: How Carrick won the Man United job and lost it again

- Carlisle: Pochettino leaves USMNT with job half-finished

After briefly failing with Rangnick's gegenpressing, they asked Erik ten Hag to find some middle ground between possession and defense. When this shockingly proved difficult, they asked Ruben Amorim, with his rigid 3-5-2 formation, to do the same. Just as he was establishing strong underlying numbers and advanced stats -- another aspect that successful modern clubs long ago began to rely on, including a Brentford team that spends infinitely less than United and earned more points over the past 2½ seasons -- Amorim was pushed out the door in favor of another favorite son, Michael Carrick.

Now Carrick's gone, too.

The tenures are getting shorter and shorter, the wins fewer and further between.

Throw in Rangnick's unhappy time (1.48 PPG) as half-season interim between Solskjaer and ten Hag, and three of the four shortest and least successful United tenures have come in the past four hires (and five years). Shockingly, returns diminish when you never establish a plan, and the initial rumored candidates list for replacing Carrick -- the passion-and-pressing Mauricio Pochettino, the far more defensive Antonio Conte and Eddie Howe, the almost van Gaal-like Julian Nagelsmann -- didn't exactly hint at a clear plan this time around, either.

articles.headline: Oklahoma City visits Sacramento following Gilgeous-Alexander's 40-point game
articles.description: Oklahoma City Thunder (8-5, eighth in the Western Conference) vs. Sacramento Kings (1-11, 14th in the Western Conference)
articles.headlineJa: ギルジャス＝アレクサンダーが40得点を記録したオクラホマシティがサクラメントに乗り込む
articles.descriptionJa: オクラホマシティ・サンダー（8勝5敗、西カンファレンス8位）対 サクラメント・キングス（1勝11敗、西カンファレンス14位）
articles.body:
Oklahoma City Thunder (8-5, eighth in the Western Conference) vs. Sacramento Kings (1-11, 14th in the Western Conference)


              Sacramento, California; Sunday, 9 p.m. EST


              BOTTOM LINE: Oklahoma City plays the Sacramento Kings after Shai Gilgeous-Alexander scored 40 points in the Thunder's 113-112 loss to the Los Angeles Clippers.


              The Kings have gone 1-9 against Western Conference teams. Sacramento is 1-8 in games decided by 10 points or more.


              The Thunder are 5-5 against Western Conference opponents. Oklahoma City ranks eighth in the Western Conference with 11.5 offensive rebounds per game led by Chet Holmgren averaging 4.7.


              The Kings make 45.5% of their shots from the field this season, which is 3.8 percentage points higher than the Thunder have allowed to their opponents (41.7%). The Kings average 111.2 points per game, 9.7 fewer points than the 120.9 the Kings allow.


              TOP PERFORMERS: Domantas Sabonis is averaging 14.5 points, 13.2 rebounds and 5.8 assists for the Kings. Darius Acuff Jr. is averaging 26.0 points over the last 10 games.


              Gilgeous-Alexander is averaging 30.5 points and 4.5 assists for the Thunder. Jared McCain is averaging 14.8 points over the past 10 games.


              LAST 10 GAMES: Kings: 1-9, averaging 108.2 points, 39.5 rebounds, 25.7 assists, 7.8 steals and 4.0 blocks per game while shooting 45.8% from the field. Their opponents have averaged 120.2 points per game.

articles.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Real Madrid tracking Bayern Munich star Michael Olise
articles.description: Real Madrid remain keen on Bayern Munich star Michael Olise. Transfer Talk has the latest.
articles.headlineJa: 移籍の噂とニュース：レアル・マドリードがバイエルン・ミュンヘンのスター、マイケル・オリーズを注視
articles.descriptionJa: レアル・マドリードはバイエルン・ミュンヘンのスター、マイケル・オリーズへの関心を維持している。Transfer Talkが最新情報をお届けする。
articles.body:
Bayern Munich star Michael Olise is still being tailed by Real Madrid, while United States internationals Folarin Balogun and Alex Freeman could be following coach Mauricio Pochettino to Manchester United. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Real Madrid remain interested in Bayern Munich winger Michael Olise, after previously being linked with him during the summer, according to L'Equipe. The 24-year-old is reported to have multiple top clubs in Europe 'dreaming' of signing him next summer, when he will enter the final two years of his contract at the Allianz Arena. Olise scored in France's 3-1 Nations League defeat against Italy on Thursday.

- Manchester United have added United States duo Folarin Balogun and Alex Freeman to their list, TEAMtalk reports. Monaco striker Balogun, 25, and Villarreal defender Freeman, 22, are seen as two ideal candidates to land in January due to their familiarity with the USMNT coach Mauricio Pochettino. It was announced on Friday that Pochettino has agreed a deal to become the next manager at United and replace the fired Michael Carrick at Old Trafford. The Red Devils have been monitoring Freeman for some time, but could now step up their interest following his impressive performances under Pochettino for the USMNT. Balogun has said that he will look to seal a move away from Monaco in the next transfer window, having seen his proposed move to Everton fall through in the summer.

- Liverpool are keen on Brighton & Hove Albion defender Luka Vuskovic, Florian Plettenberg reports. The Reds are monitoring the 19-year-old regularly after placing him on their shortlist of options for next summer, and he could be seen as a potential long term successor to Virgil van Dijk, who is yet to sign an extension on his current deal which is set to expire in June. There is no release clause in Vuskovic's contract, with his transfer expected to require a proposal worth in the region of €100 million.

- Chelsea right back Malo Gusto is attracting interest from Manchester City and Manchester United, according to talkSPORT. Both clubs are keeping tabs on the situation of the 23-year-old, who has only made three starts in the Premier League this season. The Blues would demand an offer worth £75 million before agreeing to part ways with him, in a deal that could see Gusto reunite with former manager Enzo Maresca at the Etihad Stadium.

- Juventus are interested in Tottenham Hotspur's Destiny Udogie and Barcelona's Alejandro Balde as new left backs,according to Corriere dello Sport. Udogie, 23, has made just two starts in the Premier League this season as the second choice option to Andy Robertson, and he has been identified as a player that the Bianconeri could acquire to reinforce the left side of their defense in January. Balde, 23, has also struggled to garner first team minutes and is linked with an exit from Camp Nou.

articles.headline: Borussia Dortmund to end controversial sponsorship with arms manufacturer
articles.description: Borussia Dortmund says it won't renew a sponsorship deal with Germany's largest arms manufacturer Rheinmetall, which drew criticism from fans.
articles.body:
Borussia Dortmund says it won't renew a sponsorship deal with Germany's largest arms manufacturer Rheinmetall, which drew criticism from fans as soon as it was signed.

The official sponsorship agreement between the German club and Rheinmetall, which has been in place since 2024, expires on June, 30, 2027.

- Dortmund fans use dummy tank to protest arms-maker deal

Club chairman Carsten Cramer said in an interview published on the club's website Friday that members had voted at the 2024 annual general meeting on a motion not to extend the partnership deal beyond 2027.

"Naturally, we took that into account in our discussions with Rheinmetall and treated it seriously," he said. "We are, of course, aware that our partnership has been controversial from the outset."

When the deal was signed, German media reported it was worth up to €9 million ($10 million) per year.

"From summer 2027, we will lose the income from the sponsorship agreement," Cramer said. "That is a fact. It reduces our financial room for manoeuvre. We will have to reprioritize planned investments and carefully examine how we can find viable solutions."

Rheinmetall is a "champion partner" and Dortmund displays the company's banner on advertising hoardings during games.

The agreement has caused friction among supporters to varying degrees, with some Dortmund fans even going so far as to renounce their support.

Founded in 1889 as "Rheinische Metallwaaren- und Maschinenfabrik Actiengesellschaft," Rheinmetall was one of Germany's biggest armaments manufacturers during both World Wars. It made use of forced labor during World War II.

articles.headline: Recap: USMNT's Pochettino in tears as he agrees to join Man United
articles.description: USMNT head coach Mauricio Pochettino is leaving to join Manchester United. Read all the news, analysis and reaction from ESPN.
articles.body:
United States men's national team head coach Mauricio Pochettino will leave his post and become Manchester United manager, it was announced on Friday.

Just over 24 hours after United sacked Michael Carrick, the club already has a new manager on the way. Pochettino will manage the USMNT's upcoming Concacaf Nations League games against Haiti, and his first game in charge at United will be at arch-rivals Liverpool on Nov. 22.

It means Pochettino, who has previously enjoyed coaching spells at Tottenham Hotspur, Paris Saint-Germain and Chelsea, is back in the Premier League.

Read all the news, analysis and reaction from ESPN.
